notes:
- Import from notes: paste the passwords you keep in Notes or a text file, in whatever shape you wrote them. Lockwell shows every line beside what it became (name, username, password, website, API token, SSH key), marks anything it is not sure of, and imports only once every line is read or left out.
- Bring your passwords: drop exports from Google, Apple Passwords, 1Password, Bitwarden, KeePass and others at once. Lockwell names where each came from, shows one preview, merges duplicates and reminds you to delete the exported files.
- New password for this site: in the Panel, type the site and press Return. Lockwell makes a strong password, copies it and saves the login straight away, so you only paste it into the sign-up form. Command N adds any kind of item, a token or a key as well as a login.
- One vault on two Macs: keep a vault in an iCloud Drive or Google Drive folder and open it on both. Lockwell picks up changes from the other Mac and merges them, and nothing either side wrote is lost.
- Scripts and AI agents can use a secret by name with `lockwell run`, after you allow it, without the value ever showing. Off until you turn it on in Settings, Security.
- SSH keys keep their line breaks.
